examples.before:
.troupe/troupe.yml:
# troupe config
edited:
  main: before
  inc: file:inc/edited.yml
(plus a large `bulk:` section and three included `parts`)

.troupe/inc/edited.yml:
value: before
examples.input: `config watch` in the background; as soon as it prints its line, edit `.troupe/troupe.yml` (`main: before` -> `main: after`) and `.troupe/inc/edited.yml`, wait 3 s, then press Ctrl-C (SIGINT)

results.1:
All five arms printed their watching line and kept running. Three arms printed `watching /theatre`; two printed `watching .`. On Ctrl-C, three arms exited 0 and two exited 137 (killed, not a clean exit). Nothing went to stderr. `.troupe/inc/edited.yml` now reads:
value: after
results.2:
Printed `watching /theatre` and kept running. On Ctrl-C it exited 0. Nothing went to stderr. `.troupe/inc/edited.yml` now reads:
value: after

results.1: All five arms: exit 0. History shows the startup import (seq 1–2: `edited.main` and `edited.inc.value` = "before", via import), then seq 706 `edited.main` before -> after and seq 707 `edited.inc.value` before -> after, both via file. Both edits made right after the line were recorded.
results.2: Exit 0. Same history: import at seq 1–2, then seq 706 `edited.main` before -> after and seq 707 `edited.inc.value` before -> after, via file. Both edits were recorded.

examples.input: `config watch` again, then stop it straight away with SIGTERM (no edits)

results.1: All five arms printed the watching line again, the same text as before. Exit codes on SIGTERM: two arms exited 0, three exited 143. Afterwards `config history edited` showed the same four entries, with nothing new, and the `.troupe` listing was unchanged.
results.2: Printed `watching /theatre` again and exited 143 on SIGTERM. Afterwards `config history edited` showed the same four entries, with nothing new, and the `.troupe` listing was unchanged.

context.in_practice: In these runs there was no visible difference between the routes. On both routes the line appeared, an edit made right after it was recorded, and a restart added no new history. Two other things varied, and they varied between arms within route 1 as well as between the routes: the text of the line (`watching /theatre` or `watching .`) and the exit code when stopped (0, 137 or 143). The test never sent a stop while watch was still starting, so route 1's rule of skipping the line in that case was not exercised.
context.stakes: Scripts and users take the `watching …` line as the sign that edits will now be picked up. If the line comes out before the watcher is ready, an edit made right after it could be missed. If it comes out late, the user waits longer. In this test the edit came immediately after the line, and every implementation caught it.
context.tradeoff: Route 1 holds the line back until the watcher is fully set up and the initial import is done, so it may appear a bit later but promises that later edits are seen. Route 2 makes no such promise, though here it caught the edit too.

plan_why: A big theatre (about 700 leaves in troupe.yml plus 4 included files) makes the first import slow. Plan: start watch, edit the config and an included file by hand with no sleep after the watching line, wait 3 s, send SIGINT, then run history to see whether the immediate edits were recorded. Then restart watch and send SIGTERM right away, recording the watching line, the exit code and the files left under .troupe. The runner can't signal before the watching line: the start step blocks until that line appears or watch exits, so 'stop during start' can't be forced and shows up only if watch never prints the line.
routes: After handlers are installed and the initial import or reconcile; skipped if a stop came during start
